definition_en: a formal document granting rights, a written set of rules for an organization, or to hire a vehicle for private use
core_image: 一张盖着印章、写明权利的羊皮纸
scene: 小镇的档案馆里锁着一份古老文件。The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
sceneCN: 这里 charter 指「特许状；宪章」（第 1 个义项：授予权利的正式文件）；句意是这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。

senses.title: A document granting rights
senses.definition: a formal document that gives rights or privileges to a group or place
senses.definitionCN: 授予某团体或某地权利与特权的正式文件
senses.example: The town received its charter in the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇在中世纪获得了特许状。
senses.why: A small sheet of paper bearing a seal was enough to grant a town its freedoms.
senses.whyCN: 一张盖印的小纸片，就足以授予一座城镇自由。

senses.title: To hire a vehicle privately
senses.definition: to hire a plane, boat or bus for private use
senses.definitionCN: 为私人用途租用飞机、船只或客车
senses.example: They chartered a boat for the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们包了一艘船度过下午。
senses.why: The paper that granted a right became the written contract that granted the use of a vessel.
senses.whyCN: 授予权利的纸，变成了授予船只使用权的书面合同。

senses.title: The rules of an organization
senses.definition: a written statement of the aims and rules of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 说明某组织宗旨与规则的书面文件
senses.example: The club revised its charter last year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部去年修订了章程。
senses.why: An organization's founding document borrowed the name of the town's founding grant.
senses.whyCN: 组织的创立文件借用了城镇创立特许状的名称。

intro.en: Charter comes from the same Latin paper word as chart, through a small sheet that carried a grant.
intro.cn: charter 与 chart 同出拉丁语「纸」一词，经由承载授权的纸页而来。

items.en: Carta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carta 意为纸或书面文件。

items.en: Chartula was a small sheet used for a legal grant.
items.cn: chartula 指用于法律授权的纸页。

items.en: Chartre named a sealed grant of rights.
items.cn: chartre 指盖印的权利授予书。

items.en: English charter meant a written grant of privileges.
items.cn: 英语 charter 指书面授予的特权。

items.en: The word now also names founding rules and the hiring of a vehicle.
items.cn: 如今该词还指创始章程与交通工具的包租。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the carta root, while the meaning group lists documents and hiring words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 carta 词根，近义组列出文件与租用类词。

normal.en: Charter and chart are siblings from Latin carta, a sheet of paper.
normal.cn: charter 与 chart 是拉丁语 carta（纸页）的兄弟。

normal.en: A charter is a paper that grants, whether rights or a whole boat.
normal.cn: charter 是一张授予东西的纸，授予权利或整艘船都行。

normal.en: The UN Charter is the founding paper of a world body.
normal.cn: the UN Charter 是一个世界组织的创立文件。

normal.en: A charter flight is a plane hired by one group.
normal.cn: charter flight 是一个团体包下的飞机。

normal.en: The verb charter puts the paper into action, as in charter a bus.
normal.cn: 动词 charter 让这张纸动起来，如 charter a bus。

intro.cn: charter 在 chartered 与 charterer 中保留 cart-「纸」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin carta and chartula are the paper and the small grant sheet behind charter.

definition_en: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them, or to try hard to obtain something
core_image: 一个人沿着地上的脚印拼命奔跑
scene: 狗从院门冲出去追一只野兔。The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 chase 指「追赶」（第 1 个义项：追着某人或某物跑）；句意是狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。

senses.title: To run after someone
senses.definition: to run after a person or animal in order to catch them
senses.definitionCN: 追在人或动物后面以便抓住
senses.example: The dog chased a rabbit across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着一只野兔跑过田野。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try to seize, and running after prey is that attempt in motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为试图抓住，追着猎物跑正是这种企图在移动。

senses.title: To try to obtain something
senses.definition: to try hard to get something such as money, success or a person
senses.definitionCN: 努力获得金钱、成功或某个人
senses.example: He spent years chasing a dream.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了多年追求一个梦想。
senses.why: The hunt for prey became a hunt for goals that cannot be caught by hand.
senses.whyCN: 对猎物的追捕，变成了对手无法用手抓住的目标的追逐。

senses.title: An act of pursuing
senses.definition: the act of running after someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 追在某人或某物后面的行为
senses.example: The police gave up the chase.
senses.exampleCN: 警方放弃了追逐。
senses.why: The verb's action turned into a noun, so the pursuit itself became a chase.
senses.whyCN: 动词的动作转成名词，追逐本身便成了一个 chase。

intro.en: Chase comes from a Latin verb of trying to seize, through Old French chacier.
intro.cn: chase 源自拉丁语表示试图抓住的动词，经古法语 chacier 传来。

items.en: Captare meant to try to catch or seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 captare 意为试图抓住或夺取。

items.en: Captiare carried the hunting sense into popular speech.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 captiare 把追猎义带入日常口语。

items.en: Chacier meant to hunt or drive away.
items.cn: chacier 意为追猎或赶走。

items.en: English chase first meant to hunt animals.
items.cn: 英语 chase 最初指追猎动物。

items.en: The word now covers car chases and the pursuit of aims.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖汽车追逐与对目标的追求。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chase stem, while the meaning group lists pursuing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chase 词干，近义组列出追捕类动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that chases
the act of running after
more than one chase
to follow in order to catch

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the seize root, the car chase phrase and the pursuit of a dream.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「抓住」词根、短语 car chase 以及追梦义。

normal.en: Chase and catch share an old idea of seizing, since one leads to the other.
normal.cn: chase 与 catch 共享古老的「抓住」之意，因为前者通向后者。

normal.en: Chase after is the phrase for both a runaway dog and a distant goal.
normal.cn: chase after 既用于跑掉的狗，也用于遥远的目标。

normal.en: Give chase means to start running after, not to hand something over.
normal.cn: give chase 意为开始追赶，而不是把东西交出去。

normal.en: Chase away reverses the direction and means to drive off.
normal.cn: chase away 把方向反过来，意为赶走。

normal.en: A car chase fills the screen with motion and noise.
normal.cn: car chase 用动作与噪声填满银幕。

abstract.en: Picture a dog cutting a straight line through tall grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗在深草中划出一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a runner reaching for a finish line that keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者伸手去够一条不断移动的终点线。

abstract.en: Picture two cars flashing through a wet tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象两辆车在潮湿的隧道里飞驰。

examples.en: The cat chased the ball under the sofa.
examples.cn: 猫把球追到了沙发底下。

examples.en: Reporters chased the story for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者追这条新闻追了好几周。

examples.en: He gave up the chase after two blocks.
examples.cn: 他追了两条街就放弃了。

dict_mnemonic.text: chase 与 catch 同源感：追（chase）的最终目的，就是抓（catch）到。

root: 源自拉丁语 captare（试图抓住），经晚期拉丁语 captiare 与古法语 chacier 进入英语；与 catch 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Trying to seize gives the physical pursuit, then the pursuit of aims, then the name of the pursuit itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 试图抓住先给出身体上的追赶，再给出对目标的追求，最后给出追逐这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner closing in on prey.
core.cn: 核心意象：奔跑者逐渐逼近猎物。

branches.en: A dog chases a rabbit to catch it.
branches.cn: 狗追野兔是为了抓住它。

branches.en: A dream is chased without any physical prey.
branches.cn: 追梦并没有实体的猎物。

branches.en: The chase itself becomes a thing to name.
branches.cn: 追逐本身成了一个可以被命名的东西。

branches.en: The verb and noun describe one continuous action.
branches.cn: 动词与名词描述同一个连续动作。

branches.en: Prey and goals are both things to run after.
branches.cn: 猎物与目标都是要追的东西。

intro.en: Chase forms chaser and chasing, and the collocation chase away reverses the direction.
intro.cn: chase 构成 chaser 与 chasing，搭配 chase away 则把方向反过来。

latinIntro.en: Latin captare is the seizing verb behind chase and catch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 captare 是 chase 与 catch 背后的「抓取」动词。

items.example: The film has two long chases.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影有两段长长的追逐戏。

items.example: Captare is the old hunting verb.
items.exampleCN: captare 是古老的追猎动词。

items.meaning: to follow in order to reach
items.exampleCN: 他们继续推进这个计划。

latinEntries.exampleCN: captare 给出法语 chacier。
chacier 以 chase 进入英语。

definition_en: to talk in a friendly and informal way, or a friendly informal conversation
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子随意地说笑
scene: 午后咖啡馆里两个人低声说话。They sat and chatted for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 chat 指「聊天」（第 1 个义项：轻松随意地交谈）；句意是他们坐着聊了一个小时。

senses.title: To talk casually
senses.definition: to talk in a friendly and informal way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好而随意的方式交谈
senses.example: They sat and chatted for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐着聊了一个小时。
senses.why: Chat is a shortened chatter, the sound of quick light talk.
senses.whyCN: chat 是 chatter 的缩短，后者指轻快话语的声音。

senses.title: A friendly conversation
senses.definition: a friendly and informal conversation
senses.definitionCN: 友好而随意的谈话
senses.example: We had a long chat about old school days.
senses.exampleCN: 我们聊了很久学生时代的旧事。
senses.why: The action of chatting became a countable thing, so one talk is one chat.
senses.whyCN: 聊天的动作变成可数之物，于是一次谈话就是一次 chat。

senses.title: To exchange messages online
senses.definition: to exchange short messages with people on the internet
senses.definitionCN: 在互联网上与人互发短消息
senses.example: She chats with friends every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚都和朋友网上聊天。
senses.why: The same easy talk moved from a table to a screen and kept its name.
senses.whyCN: 同样轻松的谈话从桌边移到屏幕上，名字保持不变。

intro.en: Chat began as a short form of chatter, the quick sound of idle talk.
intro.cn: chat 起初是 chatter 的缩短形式，即闲话轻快的声音。

items.en: Chatteren meant to talk quickly and idly.
items.cn: 中古英语 chateren 意为快速而闲散地说话。

items.en: Chat shortened the verb and kept the friendly tone.
items.cn: chat 缩短了这个动词，并保留友善的语气。

items.en: The noun chat named a light conversation.
items.cn: 名词 chat 指轻松的谈话。

items.en: Chat room and online chat extended the word to screens.
items.cn: chat room 与 online chat 把该词扩展到屏幕上。

items.en: The word now covers both spoken and typed small talk.
items.cn: 如今该词既指口头闲谈，也指打字聊天。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chatter stem, while the meaning group lists talk words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chatter 词干，近义组列出谈话类词。

to talk quickly about small things
more than one chat

a talk between people

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chatter root, the phrase have a chat and the online chat sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 chatter 词根、短语 have a chat 以及网上聊天义。

normal.en: Chat is chatter with the end cut off, just as the talk is light and short.
normal.cn: chat 是砍掉尾巴的 chatter，正如这种谈话轻而短。

normal.en: Have a chat turns the verb into a countable meeting.
normal.cn: have a chat 把动词变成一次可数的会面。

normal.en: Chat about is the pattern for naming the topic.
normal.cn: chat about 是说出话题的句式。

normal.en: An online chat happens without any sound at all.
normal.cn: online chat 完全没有声音。

normal.en: The adjective chatty describes a person who chats easily.
normal.cn: 形容词 chatty 形容容易聊起来的人。

abstract.en: Picture two cups cooling on a table between two talkers.
abstract.cn: 想象两个说话人之间，桌上两只杯子慢慢变凉。

abstract.en: Picture a phone screen filling with short grey bubbles.
abstract.cn: 想象手机屏幕被短短的灰色气泡填满。

abstract.en: Picture a group laughing at the door of a shop.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人在店门口说笑。

examples.en: We chatted about the match on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上我们聊了那场比赛。

examples.en: Come in for a chat when you have time.
examples.cn: 有时间进来聊聊天。

examples.en: He spends the evening chatting with friends online.
examples.cn: 他整晚都在网上和朋友聊天。

dict_mnemonic.text: chat 就是 chatter 的缩短：话多而轻松，正是聊天的样子。

root: 由中古英语 chatteren（快速闲谈）缩短而来，原为拟声词，模拟轻快话语的声音，后指轻松的交谈。

sensesIntro.en: Quick idle sound becomes the act of talking, then one conversation, then typed talk on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 轻快的闲话声先变成交谈动作，再变成一次谈话，最后变成屏幕上的打字交谈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people talking easily with no purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人没有目的地轻松交谈。

branches.en: To chat is to talk without a fixed aim.
branches.cn: 聊天就是没有固定目的地说话。

branches.en: A chat is one such talk, countable and short.
branches.cn: a chat 是其中一次谈话，可数而短小。

branches.en: Online chat moves the same ease onto a screen.
branches.cn: 网上聊天把同样的轻松移到屏幕上。

branches.en: The verb and noun share one friendly tone.
branches.cn: 动词与名词共享同一种友善语气。

branches.en: Spoken and typed chats both build contact.
branches.cn: 口头与打字聊天都在建立联系。

intro.en: Chat forms chatty and chatter, and doubles its final t before -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: chat 构成 chatty 与 chatter，并在 -ed 与 -ing 前双写词尾 t。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, echoing the sound of quick talk rather than a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 该词是英语本土词，模拟快速说话的声音，而非来自拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 孩子们叽叽喳喳说个不停。

definition_en: to act dishonestly in order to gain an advantage, or a person who does this
core_image: 考场上把答案写在小纸条上的人
scene: 考场里静得能听见笔尖沙沙作响。He tried to cheat in the final exam and was caught at once.
sceneCN: 这里 cheat 指「作弊」（第 1 个义项：在考试或比赛中用不正当手段取胜）；句意是他想在期末考试中作弊，当场就被抓住了。

senses.title: To trick someone for gain
senses.definition: to make someone believe something false so that you gain money or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信假事，从而骗取钱财或好处
senses.example: The seller cheated an old couple out of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 卖家骗走了一对老夫妇的积蓄。
senses.why: The old legal word for seizing property gave the idea of taking by unfair means.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律用语本指夺取财产，由此生出用不正当手段取得的意思。

senses.title: To act dishonestly in a test
senses.definition: to break the rules of an exam or a game in order to do better
senses.definitionCN: 为取得更好成绩而违反考试或比赛规则
senses.example: Two students were caught cheating in the midterm.
senses.exampleCN: 两名学生在期中考试中被发现作弊。
senses.why: The general sense of unfair gain narrowed to unfair gain inside a contest.
senses.whyCN: 一般意义上的不义之财缩小为比赛内部的不正当获利。

senses.title: A dishonest person
senses.definition: a person who deceives others, or a single act of deception
senses.definitionCN: 欺骗他人的人，也指一次欺骗行为
senses.example: He turned out to be a cheat who sold fake tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 原来他是个卖假票的骗子。
senses.why: English often turns an action verb into a noun that names the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动作动词转成名词，用来指做这件事的人。

intro.en: Cheat is a worn-down legal word that once meant land falling back to a lord.
intro.cn: cheat 是一个磨短的法律词，原本指归回领主的土地。

items.en: Excadere meant to fall out or fall away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 意为脱落、掉出。

items.en: Excadere named property that fell back to a lord for want of heirs.
items.cn: 该词在中世纪拉丁语中指因无继承人而归回领主的财产。

items.en: Escheat carried that legal sense into French.
items.cn: escheat 把这个法律含义带进法语。

items.en: The shortened form cheat first meant to seize property by such a claim.
items.cn: 缩略形式 cheat 最初指以这类名目夺取财产。

items.en: The sense widened to any dishonest gain, then to a dishonest person.
items.cn: 词义扩展到一切不义之财，再转指行骗的人。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps a short similar spelling, while the meaning group names acts of dishonesty.
note.cn: 形近组共享相近的短拼写，近义组列出各种不诚实的行为。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cheap look-alike, the old escheat and the three fixed prepositions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用形近词 cheap、古词 escheat 以及三个固定介词。

normal.en: Cheat and cheap differ by one letter: a cheat sells you something cheap and fake.
normal.cn: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：骗子卖给你便宜却虚假的东西。

normal.en: The old word escheat meant land falling back to a lord; cheat is that word worn down.
normal.cn: 古词 escheat 指土地归回领主，cheat 就是它磨短后的样子。

normal.en: Cheat in an exam, cheat at cards, cheat on a test: each preposition marks its own scene.
normal.cn: cheat in an exam、cheat at cards、cheat on a test，每个介词都标出自己的场景。

normal.en: A cheat is a person and cheating is the act, while cheater is the plain agent noun.
normal.cn: a cheat 指人，cheating 指行为，cheater 则是最直白的施动名词。

normal.en: Cheat death is the one flattering phrase: it means to escape death narrowly.
normal.cn: cheat death 是唯一带褒义的搭配，意为死里逃生。

abstract.en: Picture a corner of a small answer note slipping out of a sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象一小角答案纸条从袖口滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand swapping one card under a card table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在牌桌下换掉一张牌。

abstract.en: Picture a man whispering low prices for fake tickets at a station gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在车站门口低声兜售假票。

examples.en: He cheated the company out of a large sum.
examples.cn: 他骗走了公司一大笔钱。

examples.en: The teacher warned us never to cheat.
examples.cn: 老师警告我们绝不要作弊。

examples.en: A cheat never keeps friends for long.
examples.cn: 骗子留不住朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: cheat 与 cheap 只差一个字母：便宜货里最容易藏着骗局。

root: 源自拉丁语 excadere（脱落），经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 escheat（无嗣归公的土地）缩略为 cheat，本指以不正当名目取得财产。

sensesIntro.en: The seizure of property gives the general sense of dishonest gain, which narrows to exam rooms and then shifts to the person.
sensesIntro.cn: 对财产的夺取给出「不义之财」的总义，随后缩小到考场，最后转到行骗的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand hiding an answer note inside a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：把答案纸条藏在袖子里的那只手。

branches.en: A seller takes money by telling a lie.
branches.cn: 卖家靠说谎拿走钱财。

branches.en: The exam room is where the unfair gain happens.
branches.cn: 考场是不正当获利发生的场所。

branches.en: The same word then names the person who lies.
branches.cn: 同一个词随后指说谎的那个人。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a hidden unfair move.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「暗中不正当操作」的意思。

branches.en: Cheating in a test earns the label cheat.
branches.cn: 在考试中作弊就会得到 cheat 这个称呼。

intro.en: One short root serves the verb, the noun and every derived form of cheat.
intro.cn: 一个短词根支撑 cheat 的动词、名词与全部派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin excadere and Old French escheat stand behind the modern word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excadere 与古法语 escheat 是现代这个词的前身。

items.example: They cheated on the last quiz.
The cheated buyers sued the shop.
items.exampleCN: 受骗的买家起诉了这家店。

items.example: Escheat was a medieval legal term.
items.exampleCN: escheat 是中世纪的法律术语。

latinEntries.meaning: to fall out or fall away
latinEntries.example: Excadere is the remote base of cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excadere 是 cheat 的远源词基。

latinEntries.meaning: property falling back to a lord
latinEntries.example: Escheat lost its first sound to become cheat.
latinEntries.exampleCN: escheat 丢掉首音后变成 cheat。

definition_en: to examine something to make sure it is correct or safe, or an examination of this kind
core_image: 拿着一份清单逐项打勾的手
scene: 出发前屋里还亮着灯。She checked the list twice before leaving the house.
sceneCN: 这里 check 指「核对」（第 1 个义项：逐项查看是否正确）；句意是她出门前把清单核对了两遍。

senses.title: To examine and confirm
senses.definition: to look at something carefully in order to see whether it is correct or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，判断其是否正确或安全
senses.example: Please check your answers before handing in the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 交卷之前请核对你的答案。
senses.why: A chess warning asked a player to look at the board at once, and looking closely became the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 棋盘上的警告要求棋手立刻查看局势，仔细查看便成了核心义。

senses.title: To stop or slow something
senses.definition: to stop or slow the progress of something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 阻止或减缓有害事物的发展
senses.example: The new rules are meant to check the spread of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定旨在阻止火势蔓延。
senses.why: Blocking the king in chess turned into the general idea of holding something back.
senses.whyCN: 在国际象棋中挡住国王，转化为一般意义上的「拦住」。

senses.title: A bank order
senses.definition: a printed order telling a bank to pay money from an account
senses.definitionCN: 指示银行从账户付款的印刷单据
senses.example: He paid the rent by check.
senses.exampleCN: 他用支票付了房租。
senses.why: The word also named a written order that could be checked against a bank account.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指可向银行账户核对兑现的书面命令。

intro.en: Check began as the chess cry that warned a king he was in danger.
intro.cn: check 最初是国际象棋里提醒国王处境危险的一声喊。

items.en: Shah meant king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王。

items.en: The cry al-shah warned that the king was threatened.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语中的喊声提示国王受到威胁。

items.en: Eschec named the chess move that attacked the king.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 指攻击国王的那一步棋。

items.en: English check first meant a chess threat to the king.
items.cn: 英语 check 最初指棋局中对国王的威胁。

items.en: The word widened to any sudden stop, then to inspection and to a bank order.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何突然的制止，再扩展到查看与银行票据。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound or one letter, while the meaning group lists acts of careful looking.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音或一个字母，近义组列出仔细查看的动作。

entries.definition: a bank order spelled the British way
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写的银行付款单

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: to look at something in detail
to look at something officially for faults
to prove that something is true

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chess origin, three everyday phrases with check and the British spelling cheque.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用国际象棋来源、三个含 check 的日常搭配以及英式拼写 cheque。

normal.en: The chess word check shouted that a king was in danger, and English kept the shout.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的 check 高喊国王有危险，英语把这声喊留了下来。

normal.en: Check the list, check in, check out: three daily phrases all involve confirming something.
normal.cn: check the list、check in、check out，三个日常搭配都涉及确认。

normal.en: Cheque is the British spelling of the same sound, used only for the bank order.
normal.cn: cheque 是同一读音的英式拼写，只用于银行付款单。

normal.en: To check a fire is to hold it back, the old chess sense of blocking a king.
normal.cn: to check a fire 是把火拦住，正是旧日棋局中挡住国王的意思。

normal.en: Checklist and check-in are compounds built directly from the verb stem.
normal.cn: checklist 与 check-in 都是直接从动词词干构成的复合词。

abstract.en: Picture a finger moving down a paper list, ticking one line at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿纸上的清单下移，一行行打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece halted just before it reaches the king.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子冲到国王面前却被挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a bank clerk sliding a printed slip across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象银行职员把一张印刷单据从柜台推过来。

examples.en: She checked the door twice before going to bed.
examples.cn: 她睡前把门检查了两遍。

examples.en: The doctor will check your eyes tomorrow.
examples.cn: 医生明天会检查你的眼睛。

examples.en: A firm answer can check a rumour at once.
examples.cn: 坚定的答复能立刻止住谣言。

dict_mnemonic.text: check 与 chess 同源：棋盘上一声「将军」，就是把对方的行动拦下来。

root: 源自波斯语 shah（国王），经阿拉伯语与古法语 eschec 进入英语，本为国际象棋中「将军」的警告声。

sensesIntro.en: The warning cry gives the idea of a sudden stop, which splits into careful looking and into holding something back.
sensesIntro.cn: 警告的喊声给出「突然制止」的意思，随后分出仔细查看与加以拦阻两条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice calling out that the king must be watched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声喊出「看好国王」的提醒。

branches.en: Looking closely grew out of the demand to watch the board.
branches.cn: 仔细查看源自「看好棋盘」的要求。

branches.en: Stopping a fire repeats the old blocking move.
branches.cn: 阻止火势沿用了旧日拦挡的动作。

branches.en: A bank order is checked against an account before it is paid.
branches.cn: 银行票据付款前要对着账户核对。

branches.en: Both senses keep the energy of a sudden halt.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了「骤然停住」的力度。

branches.en: Inspection and the paper order share one written word.
branches.cn: 查看与纸质票据共用一个书写形式。

intro.en: Check stays a single short stem across its verb, noun and compound forms.
intro.cn: check 在动词、名词与复合形式中始终保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem reaches back through Old French eschec to Persian shah, the word for a king.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干经古法语 eschec 上溯到波斯语 shah，即国王。

items.example: She is checking the list now.
The pilot ran through the checklist.

items.exampleCN: 检查员发现了一个错误。

items.meaning: the act of registering on arrival

items.example: She wrote a cheque for the rent.
items.exampleCN: 她开了一张付房租的支票。

latinEntries.meaning: the chess threat to a king
latinEntries.exampleCN: eschec 进入英语后写作 check。

latinEntries.example: Shah is the oldest layer of check.
latinEntries.exampleCN: shah 是 check 最古老的一层。

definition_zh: n. 厨师长，主厨；技艺高超的厨师
definition_en: the head cook who runs a professional kitchen; a skilled cook
core_image: 白色高帽下一个人低头尝汤
scene: 主厨尝了一口汤，又加了一撮盐。The chef tasted the soup and added a pinch of salt.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chef 指主厨；句意是主厨尝汤后又加了一撮盐。

senses.title: Head cook
senses.definition: the head cook who runs a professional kitchen
senses.definitionCN: 掌管专业厨房的厨师长
senses.example: The chef checks every plate before it leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 主厨在每盘菜出厨房前逐一检查。
senses.why: French chef meant simply the head of something.
senses.whyCN: 法语 chef 本意只是某事的「头」。

senses.title: A skilled cook
senses.definition: any skilled cook, especially one in charge of a kitchen
senses.definitionCN: 任何手艺高超的厨师，尤指掌管厨房者
senses.example: He is a fine chef at home too.
senses.exampleCN: 他在家里也是个好厨师。
senses.why: English narrowed the French word to the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个法语词的适用范围收窄到厨房。

intro.en: Chef is French for head, short for chef de cuisine, the head of the kitchen.
intro.cn: chef 在法语里就是「头」，是 chef de cuisine（厨房之首）的简称。

items.en: Caput means a head.
items.cn: caput 意为头。

items.en: Chief means head or leader.
items.cn: chief 意为头或首领。

items.en: Chef de cuisine means head of the kitchen.
items.cn: chef de cuisine 意为厨房之首。

items.en: English borrows chef for a head cook.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语借入 chef 指厨师长。

items.en: The title spreads through professional kitchens.
items.cn: 二十世纪传遍专业厨房。

items.en: Chef also means any skilled cook.
items.cn: 现代也指技艺高超的厨师。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chef sound; the near-meaning group names kitchen roles.
note.cn: 形近组与 chef 读音或词源相近；近义组列出厨房里的角色。

entries.definition: A leader.
A clan leader.
To rub until sore.
A person who prepares food.
A person who bakes bread.
A person who cuts meat.

normalIntro.en: The chef is the head of the kitchen, as the word itself says.
normalIntro.cn: chef 这个词本身就说清楚了：厨房之首。

normal.en: Caput means a head.
normal.cn: caput 意为头。

normal.en: French chef also means head.
normal.cn: 法语 chef 也意为头。

normal.en: Chef de cuisine is head of the kitchen.
normal.cn: chef de cuisine 是厨房之首。

normal.en: English kept the short form.
normal.cn: 英语留下了简称。

normal.en: A chef runs the line.
normal.cn: 主厨统管整个出菜线。

abstract.en: A white hat with authority.
abstract.cn: 带着权威的白帽子。

abstract.en: The person who tastes last.
abstract.cn: 最后尝味的人。

abstract.en: A kitchen with one voice.
abstract.cn: 只有一个声音的厨房。

examples.en: The chef sharpened his knife before service.
examples.cn: 主厨在开餐前磨好刀。

examples.en: A pastry chef made the wedding cake.
examples.cn: 一位糕点主厨做了婚礼蛋糕。

examples.en: The chef refused to serve cold soup.
examples.cn: 主厨拒绝上冷汤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歇福」——歇下来有口福，全靠主厨。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）→ 古法语 chief → chef de cuisine → 英语 chef

sensesIntro.en: The head of the kitchen kept the French name for head.
sensesIntro.cn: 厨房之首沿用了法语里「头」这个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall white hat bent over a steaming pan
core.cn: 核心意象：白色高帽俯在冒热气的锅上

branches.en: A tasting spoon lifted from a pan.
branches.cn: 从锅里抬起的一把尝味勺。

branches.en: A row of plates checked one by one.
branches.cn: 逐盘检查的一排出菜。

branches.en: A Sunday kitchen full of steam.
branches.cn: 周日蒸汽腾腾的厨房。

branches.en: A friend who cooks for the whole table.
branches.cn: 为全桌做饭的朋友。

branches.en: The person whose taste decides.
branches.cn: 由他一口定味的人。

intro.en: Chef keeps a Latin word for head; the list below adds words of headship and cooking.
intro.cn: chef 保留了拉丁语「头」一词；下面列出首领与烹饪词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput is a head and culina is a kitchen.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头，culina 意为厨房。

latinEntries.exampleCN: caput 产生 capital 与 chef。
culina 产生 culinary 与 kiln。
coquere 产生 concoct 与 biscuit。

definition_en: relating to chemistry, or a substance produced by or used in chemistry
core_image: 实验台上排成一列的试剂瓶
scene: 实验室里通风柜嗡嗡作响。The chemical reaction turned the liquid from clear to blue.
sceneCN: 这里 chemical 指「化学的」（第 1 个义项：与化学有关的）；句意是这一化学反应使液体由澄清变成蓝色。

senses.title: Relating to chemistry
senses.definition: connected with chemistry or with the substances and changes it studies
senses.definitionCN: 与化学或化学研究的物质与变化有关的
senses.example: The chemical reaction released a great deal of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个化学反应释放出大量热。
senses.why: The adjective was built from the old name of the art of transforming matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由那门「转化物质之术」的古老名称构成。

senses.title: A substance made by chemistry
senses.definition: a substance produced by or used in chemical processes
senses.definitionCN: 由化学过程产生或用于化学过程的物质
senses.example: Farmers must store chemicals away from water.
senses.exampleCN: 农民必须把化学制品存放在远离水源的地方。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the things it describes, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指它所描述的东西，这在英语中很常见。

intro.en: Chemical descends from the old art of alchemy, whose name travelled through Arabic.
intro.cn: chemical 源自古老的炼金术，其名称经阿拉伯语辗转而来。

items.en: Khemeia named the art of transforming metals.
items.cn: 希腊语 khemeia 指转化金属的技艺。

items.en: Al-kimiya carried that art into Arabic learning.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 把这门技艺带入阿拉伯学术。

items.en: Alchimia named the same art in Europe.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 在欧洲指同一门技艺。

items.en: Chemical first meant belonging to this art.
items.cn: chemical 最初意为属于这门技艺的。

items.en: The word now covers the science itself and the substances it handles.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指这门科学，也指它处理的物质。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chem- stem, while the meaning group lists things a laboratory handles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chem- 词干，近义组列出实验室处理的东西。

entries.definition: a scientist who works with chemistry
the science of substances and their changes
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质及其变化的科学

entries.definition: belonging to the old art of alchemy
a material with particular qualities
a substance formed from two or more elements
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或多种元素形成的物质

entries.definition: made by chemical industry rather than nature
entries.definitionCN: 由化学工业而非自然生成的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the chem- stem, the alchemy history and the everyday compound chemicals.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 chem- 词干、炼金术历史以及日常复合词 chemicals。

normal.en: Chemical, chemist and chemistry all stand on the same four letters chem.
normal.cn: chemical、chemist、chemistry 都站在同样的四个字母 chem 上。

normal.en: Chemical is the adjective, chemicals are the bottles a lab stores.
normal.cn: chemical 是形容词，chemicals 则是实验室存放的一瓶瓶东西。

normal.en: Alchemy came before chemistry; the old art hides inside the modern word.
normal.cn: 炼金术早于化学，这门古老技艺就藏在这个现代词里。

normal.en: A chemical change makes a new substance; a physical change does not.
normal.cn: 化学变化产生新物质，物理变化则不产生。

normal.en: The ending -al makes an adjective, as in medical and logical.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 构成形容词，如 medical 与 logical。

abstract.en: Picture blue liquid climbing through a glass tube.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色液体沿着玻璃管往上爬。

abstract.en: Picture rows of labelled bottles behind glass doors.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃门后一排排贴好标签的瓶子。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop changing a whole beaker's colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴液体改变整只烧杯的颜色。

examples.en: The factory must treat its chemical waste before release.
examples.cn: 这家工厂必须在排放前处理化学废料。

examples.en: Some chemicals are safe in small amounts.
examples.cn: 有些化学物质少量使用时是安全的。

examples.en: A chemical change cannot be undone easily.
examples.cn: 化学变化不容易逆转。

dict_mnemonic.text: chem 是化学的词根，-al 是形容词尾巴：沾上化学的，就是化学的。

root: 源自希腊语 khemeia（转化金属之术），经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 与中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 进入英语，后缩为 chem- 词干。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective comes from the name of an old art, and the noun then names the substances that art produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词来自一门古老技艺的名称，名词随后指这门技艺产出的物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop that changes the colour of a whole beaker.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴改变整只烧杯颜色的液滴。

branches.en: The adjective describes reactions and processes.
branches.cn: 形容词描述反应与过程。

branches.en: The plural noun names stored substances.
branches.cn: 复数名词指储存的各种物质。

branches.en: Chemical change is the phrase that fixes the adjective.
branches.cn: chemical change 这一搭配固定了形容词的用法。

branches.en: The adjective and the noun differ only in ending.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词只差一个词尾。

branches.en: Harmful chemicals need careful storage.
branches.cn: 有害化学物质需要小心存放。

intro.en: Chemical joins the chem- stem to the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: chemical 把 chem- 词干与形容词词尾 -al 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The stem passed from Greek khemeia through Arabic al-kimiya into medieval Latin.

definition_en: a scientist who studies chemistry, or a person who prepares and sells medicines
core_image: 穿白大褂在药柜前配药的人
scene: 街角那家小店的招牌已经褪色。The chemist weighed the powder and sealed it in a small bottle.
sceneCN: 这里 chemist 指「药剂师」（第 2 个义项：配制并出售药物的人）；句意是药剂师称好药粉，封进一只小瓶。

senses.title: A chemistry scientist
senses.definition: a scientist who studies the composition and behaviour of substances
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质组成与变化规律的科学家
senses.example: The chemist published a paper on new polymers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位化学家发表了一篇关于新型聚合物的论文。
senses.why: The -ist ending marks a person who practises the science named by the stem.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记出从事词干所命名那门科学的人。

senses.title: A person who sells medicines
senses.definition: a person trained to prepare and sell medicines in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、在店铺里配制并出售药物的人
senses.example: Ask the chemist before mixing these pills.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些药混着吃之前先问药剂师。
senses.why: In Britain the same trained person both studies drugs and hands them over the counter.
senses.whyCN: 在英国，同一位受过训练的人既研究药物，也在柜台后把药交给顾客。

senses.title: A shop selling medicines
senses.definition: a shop where medicines and small health goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 出售药物与小型保健用品的店铺
senses.example: The chemist opens at eight on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药房工作日八点开门。
senses.why: British speech shortens the chemist's shop to the chemist, so the person's name becomes the place.

items.en: Chemist first meant a student of this art.
items.cn: chemist 最初指这门技艺的研习者。

abstract.en: Picture a hand weighing white powder on a brass scale.

definition_zh: 樱桃；樱桃树；樱桃色；樱桃木
definition_en: a small round red or dark red fruit with a single hard stone, or the tree that bears it
core_image: 枝头垂着的小红果，咬开是甜汁和一枚硬核
scene: 初夏的果园里，孩子们踮起脚尖伸手去够枝头最红的那一颗。She picked the ripest cherry from the tree and ate it on the spot.
sceneCN: 这里 cherry 是「樱桃」（第 1 个义项：樱桃树的果实）；句意是「她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了」。

pos.zh: 樱桃；樱桃树；樱桃木；樱桃色

senses.title: The edible fruit of the cherry tree
senses.definition: a small round fruit with red or dark red skin, sweet or sour flesh, and a single hard stone
senses.definitionCN: 一种小圆果，皮呈红色或深红，果肉甜或酸，中间有一枚硬核
senses.example: The cake was topped with cream and a single cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上点缀着奶油和一颗樱桃。
senses.why: The word names the fruit itself, so the core image is the round red berry hanging on the branch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指的就是果实本身，核心意象是挂在枝头的小红果。

senses.title: The tree that bears cherries
senses.definition: the tree (genus Prunus) that produces cherries, grown for fruit or for blossom
senses.definitionCN: 结樱桃的树（李属），种来收果或赏花
senses.example: They planted a cherry in the garden years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 多年前他们在花园里种了一棵樱桃树。
senses.why: English routinely extends fruit names to the plant itself, so the berry image grows into the tree.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯把果名直接延伸到果树本身，果实意象便扩展成整棵树。

senses.title: The wood of the cherry tree
senses.definition: the reddish-brown timber of the cherry tree, valued for furniture and cabinets
senses.definitionCN: 樱桃树的木材，呈红棕色，常用于做家具和柜子
senses.example: The cabinet is made of solid cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个柜子是实心樱桃木做的。
senses.why: Material names in English often come from the tree source, extending the image from fruit to timber.
senses.whyCN: 英语里木材名常直接取自树名，意象从果实延伸到木材。

senses.title: A bright red colour like a cherry
senses.definition: a bright red colour resembling ripe cherries, often used of lips, paint or fabrics
senses.definitionCN: 像熟樱桃一样的鲜红色，常用来形容嘴唇、油漆或布料
senses.example: Her new scarf was a glossy cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新围巾是亮泽的樱桃红色。
senses.why: The intense red skin of the fruit becomes a colour name, a common path in colour vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 果实鲜红的果皮被借为颜色名，这是颜色词汇最常见的形成路径。

senses.title: The hymen, in informal or euphemistic use
senses.definition: in informal slang, virginity, especially in the phrase to lose one's cherry
senses.definitionCN: 在俚语中委婉指童贞，常见于 lose one's cherry 一语
senses.example: That slang sense appears mainly in very informal speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俚语义主要出现在非常口语的场合。
senses.why: The round red shape invites euphemistic slang, a figurative leap from fruit to taboo topic.
senses.whyCN: 红圆的果形引发了委婉俚语，从果实意象跳跃到禁忌话题。

senses.title: The best part or prize, in figurative use
senses.titleCN: 精华；最好的部分（比喻用法）
senses.definition: figuratively, the best or most attractive thing, as in the cherry on the cake
senses.definitionCN: 比喻最精彩、最诱人的部分，如 the cherry on the cake（锦上添花之物）
senses.example: Winning the award was the cherry on top of a great season.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖是精彩赛季锦上添花的一笔。
senses.why: The sweet red fruit placed on top of a dessert stands for the finishing touch, hence the best part.
senses.whyCN: 甜点顶端那颗红樱桃象征点睛之笔，由此引申为最好的部分。

intro.en: Cherry is one of the many fruit words English borrowed through French from Latin, and the singular form was reshaped by folk etymology.
intro.cn: cherry 是英语经法语借自拉丁语的众多果名之一，其单数形式还曾被民间词源重新塑造。

items.en: Latin had cerasus (or ceresium), the cherry tree and its fruit, borrowed from Greek kerasos; the ultimate source is possibly an Anatolian language, though this is generally considered uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语有 cerasus（或 ceresium），指樱桃树及其果实，借自希腊语 kerasos；更早的来源一般认为不确定，可能出自安纳托利亚语系语言。

items.en: Latin cerasum evolved into Old French cerise, which Anglo-Norman speakers brought to England after 1066.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cerasum 演变为古法语 cerise，1066 年之后随盎格鲁-诺曼人带入英格兰。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as cherise or cheryse; because the final s was heard as a plural ending, speakers cut it off and the singular cherry was formed by mistake, a classic folk etymology.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 cherise / cheryse；词尾的 s 被误当成复数标记，人们把它剪掉，错误地造出了单数 cherry，是典型的民间词源现象。

items.en: The plural cherries was re-formed from the new singular, and the tree sense and the timber sense became established as English gardeners and cabinetmakers used the word daily.
items.cn: 复数 cherries 从新的单数重新生成，果树义和木材义随着园丁和木匠的日常使用而固定下来。

items.en: Colour names, figurative phrases such as the cherry on the cake, and the compound cherry-pick all grew from the fruit image.
items.cn: 颜色名、the cherry on the cake 等比喻短语，以及复合词 cherry-pick，都是从果实意象生长出来的。

note.en: Cherry belongs to a small family of fruit-and-tree words, and it is easy to confuse with visually similar English words.
note.cn: cherry 属于一小组「果实＋树木」词，也容易和拼写或发音相近的英语词混淆。

entries.definition: happy and cheerful in manner
entries.definitionCN: 欢快的；兴致高的——与 cherry 仅一个字母之差，词源不同

entries.definitionCN: 樱桃红——cherry 的古法语前身 cerise 直接借入英语成为颜色词

entries.definition: a small juicy fruit without a stone, such as a strawberry or blueberry

entries.definition: a soft round fruit with yellow-pink skin and a large stone
entries.definitionCN: 桃——同为核果，果形更大，也常进入比喻用法

normalIntro.en: Use the word's shape, sound and word family to lock it in.
normalIntro.cn: 用词形、读音和词族把 cherry 牢牢记住。

normal.en: cherry ends in -erry like berry and merry, a rhyming trio of small happy words.
normal.cn: cherry 词尾 -erry 与 berry（浆果）、merry（欢乐）押韵，三个轻快的小词一组。

normal.en: Old French cerise lost its s because English heard it as a plural, so cherry is cerise minus the mistaken ending.
normal.cn: 古法语 cerise 的 s 被误当复数剪掉，cherry 就是「cerise 去掉错认的词尾」。

normal.en: Plural cherries changes y to i before -es, the same spelling rule as babies and cities.
normal.cn: 复数 cherries 把 y 变 i 再加 es，规则同 babies、cities。

normal.en: Cherry blossom is the famous spring image; the tree sense lives in this phrase.
normal.cn: cherry blossom（樱花）是著名的春日意象，树的义项就藏在这个短语里。

normal.en: Cherry-pick means to take only the best, the fruit picked by hand.
normal.cn: cherry-pick 意为「只挑最好的」，即亲手摘果的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny red globe with a green stem, the exact image the word carries.
abstract.cn: 想一颗带绿梗的小红球，这正是这个词的核心画面。

abstract.en: See a cake crowned by one cherry: the finishing touch, the best part.
abstract.cn: 看蛋糕顶上那颗樱桃：点睛之笔，最好的部分。

abstract.en: Hear the rhyme cherry–berry–merry as three stones skipping on water.

examples.cn: 她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了。

examples.cn: 街道两旁种着四月开花的樱桃树。

examples.en: Being named captain was the cherry on top of a perfect season.
examples.cn: 被任命为队长是完美赛季锦上添花的一笔。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 cerasus（樱桃树／樱桃），经古法语 cerise 进入英语；拉丁语词又借自希腊语 kerasos，更早来源可能出自安纳托利亚地区的语言，具体存疑。英语把词尾 s 误当复数剪掉，形成单数 cherry，属民间词源。与 cher只是词源同源，与 cherish、cheery 仅拼写相近。

senses.definition: a large strong box with a lid, used for storing things
senses.definitionCN: 带盖的大型坚固储物箱
senses.example: The sailors kept their clothes in a wooden chest.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们把衣服放在一只木箱里。
senses.why: The oldest sense came from Greek and Latin words for a box.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示箱子的词。

senses.title: A piece of furniture with drawers
senses.definition: a piece of furniture with drawers, used for keeping clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带抽屉、用来存放衣物的家具
senses.example: The clean shirts are in the chest of drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的衬衫在五斗柜里。
senses.why: A chest of drawers is a box turned into furniture, so the short name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 五斗柜是把箱子变成家具，简短的名称便保留下来。

intro.en: Chest first meant a box, and only later borrowed the shape for the human rib cage.
intro.cn: chest 最初指箱子，后来才借这个形状指人的胸腔。

items.en: Kiste named a box for storage.
items.cn: 希腊语 kiste 指储物的箱子。

items.en: Cista named a box or a case.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cista 指箱子或匣子。

items.en: Cest named a box with a lid.
items.cn: 古英语 cest 指带盖的箱子。

items.en: The box word was transferred to the rib cage.
items.cn: 表示箱子的词被转用到肋骨围成的胸腔上。

items.en: Chest covers the body, storage boxes and chests of drawers.
items.cn: 如今 chest 涵盖身体部位、储物箱与五斗柜。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists containers and body words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出容器与身体部位词。

entries.definition: a board game of kings and queens
entries.definitionCN: 以国王与王后为棋子的棋盘游戏

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

entries.definition: a container with stiff sides and a lid
a large strong case for travel
a container made for one kind of thing
entries.definitionCN: 为某类物品制作的容器

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the box origin, the container shape of the body and the drawers idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「箱子」来源、身体的容器形状以及五斗柜的说法。

normal.en: Chest began as a box, and the ribs still make a box around the heart.
normal.cn: chest 本是箱子，而肋骨至今仍在心脏周围围成一只箱子。

normal.en: A chest of drawers is a box grown legs and handles.
normal.cn: chest of drawers 就是长出腿和把手的箱子。

normal.en: Get it off your chest: say the worry out loud and feel lighter.
normal.cn: get it off your chest：把心事说出来，就会轻松一些。

normal.en: Chest pain, chest cold, chest X-ray: medical phrases keep the body sense.
normal.cn: chest pain、chest cold、chest X-ray，这些医学搭配保留身体义。

normal.en: The plural chests adds an s to both the box and the body.
normal.cn: 复数 chests 对箱子和胸部同样只加 s。

abstract.en: Picture a brass lock catching light on an old wooden lid.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木箱盖上铜锁反着光。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat against a heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在跳动的心口。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open on folded shirts.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开，露出叠好的衬衫。

examples.en: The nurse listened to his chest and took notes.
examples.cn: 护士听了他的胸部，做了记录。

examples.en: An old chest stood at the foot of the bed.
examples.cn: 床脚放着一只旧箱子。

examples.en: She keeps her winter clothes in the chest of drawers.
examples.cn: 她把冬衣放在五斗柜里。

dict_mnemonic.text: chest 像一只箱子：木箱装东西，胸腔装心肺，抽屉柜装衣服。

root: 源自希腊语 kiste（箱子），经拉丁语 cista 与古英语 cest 进入英语，十六世纪起兼指胸腔。

sensesIntro.en: The stored box is the oldest sense, the body borrowed its shape, and the furniture borrowed its name.
sensesIntro.cn: 储物箱是最古老义项，身体借用了它的形状，家具又借用了它的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lidded container that holds something precious inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带盖、内装贵重之物的容器。

branches.en: The body sense names the rib cage.
branches.cn: 身体义项指肋骨围成的胸腔。

branches.en: The box sense keeps the lid and the lock.
branches.cn: 箱子义项保留盖与锁。

branches.en: The furniture sense adds drawers to the box.
branches.cn: 家具义项给箱子添上抽屉。

branches.en: Both senses share the container image.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享容器意象。

branches.en: A chest of drawers is a box made for a bedroom.
branches.cn: 五斗柜是为卧室改造的箱子。

intro.en: Chest stays one short stem through its plural and its two derivatives.
intro.cn: chest 在复数与两个派生词中保持同一个短词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin cista, a box, comes from Greek kiste and gives English chest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cista（箱子）来自希腊语 kiste，并给出英语的 chest。

items.meaning: the body front or a strong box

items.example: Two chests stood in the hall.
The child had a chesty cough.

items.meaning: as much as a chest holds
items.example: A chestful of old maps was found.
items.exampleCN: 发现了满满一箱旧地图。

items.example: The drawer stuck in damp weather.
items.exampleCN: 潮湿天气里抽屉会卡住。

items.meaning: one of the curved bones of the chest

items.exampleCN: cista 变成古英语的 cest。

latinEntries.example: Cista is the direct source of chest.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cista 是 chest 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Kiste is the oldest layer of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: kiste 是这个词最古老的一层。

definition_en: to crush food with the teeth before swallowing, or to think about something again and again
core_image: 闭着嘴慢慢咀嚼的人
scene: 食堂里人声嘈杂，盘子碰得叮当响。He chewed each mouthful slowly and said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 chew 指「咀嚼」（第 1 个义项：用牙齿反复嚼碎食物）；句意是他每一口都慢慢咀嚼，什么也没说。

senses.title: To crush food with the teeth
senses.definition: to break food into small pieces with the teeth before swallowing
senses.definitionCN: 吞咽之前用牙齿把食物弄碎
senses.example: Chew your food before you swallow it.
senses.exampleCN: 吞下去之前先把食物嚼碎。
senses.why: The Old English verb named the work of the jaws, and that physical sense has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词本指颌部的动作，这一身体义从未改变。

senses.title: To think something over
senses.definition: to consider an idea or a problem slowly and repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而反复地思考某个想法或问题
senses.example: He chewed over the offer for a whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个提议反复琢磨了整整一周。
senses.why: Turning food in the mouth became a picture for turning an idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 嘴里翻动食物，成了脑中翻动想法的比喻。

intro.en: Chew is an old English verb that has kept its bodily meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: chew 是一个古英语动词，一千年间一直保留着身体动作的含义。

items.en: Kewwan meant to chew or to crush with the teeth.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 kewwan 意为咀嚼或用牙弄碎。

items.en: Ceowan named the action of the jaws on food.
items.cn: 古英语 ceowan 指颌部对食物的动作。

items.en: Chewen kept the plain food sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 chewen 保留单纯的食物义。

items.en: The phrase chew over stretched the action to thinking.
items.cn: chew over 这一说法把动作延伸到思考。

items.en: Chewy and chewing gum joined the family later.
items.cn: chewy 与 chewing gum 后来加入这个词族。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- opening, while the meaning group lists ways of biting food.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 开头，近义组列出咬食物的各种方式。

entries.definition: the side of the face below the eye
a solid food made from milk
entries.definitionCN: 用牛奶制成的固体食品

entries.definition: the part of the face below the mouth
to cut into something with the teeth
to keep biting something hard
to eat something steadily and noisily

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the jaw relatives, the chew over idiom and the chewy adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用颌部同源词、chew over 习语以及形容词 chewy。

normal.en: Chew and cheek come from the same jaw area: one is the action, the other the flesh.
normal.cn: chew 与 cheek 都出自颌部：一个是动作，一个是皮肉。

normal.en: Chew over means to turn a problem in the mind as if it were food.
normal.cn: chew over 意为把问题当食物一样在脑子里翻来覆去。

normal.en: Chewy describes meat or candy that resists the teeth.
normal.cn: chewy 形容需要用牙使劲的肉或糖。

normal.en: The past tense is simply chewed, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: 过去式就是 chewed，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Chewing gum keeps the mouth busy without any food.
normal.cn: chewing gum 让嘴一直动着，却不是在吃东西。

abstract.en: Picture a man eating slowly while the table talks around him.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人慢慢吃着，桌边的人都在说话。

abstract.en: Picture a pen top flattened by nervous teeth.
abstract.cn: 想象笔帽被紧张的牙咬扁。

abstract.en: Picture a cow's jaw moving in a steady circle.
abstract.cn: 想象牛的下颌一圈圈不停地动。

examples.en: The meat was too tough to chew.
examples.cn: 这肉太硬，嚼不动。

examples.en: She chewed her sandwich while reading the report.
examples.cn: 她一边嚼三明治一边看报告。

examples.en: Give him time to chew over the plan.
examples.cn: 给他时间反复考虑这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: chew 与 cheek 同源：动的是下巴和脸颊，嚼的是嘴里的东西。

root: 源自日耳曼语 kewwan（咀嚼），古英语作 ceowan，中古英语作 chewen，身体义沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: The teeth crushing food gives the physical sense, and the same turning motion gives the mental sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 牙齿弄碎食物给出身体义，而同样的翻动动作给出心理义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: teeth working slowly on a mouthful of food.
core.cn: 核心意象：牙齿慢慢对付一口食物。

branches.en: Food is crushed before it is swallowed.
branches.cn: 食物在吞下之前被嚼碎。

branches.en: An idea is turned over the same way.
branches.cn: 一个想法也以同样方式被反复翻动。

branches.en: Chewy food resists the teeth for a while.
branches.cn: 有嚼劲的食物会让牙齿多费些力。

branches.en: Both senses share a slow repeated motion.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享缓慢重复的动作。

branches.en: Chew over keeps the food picture in the mind.
branches.cn: chew over 把食物的画面留在脑中。

intro.en: Chew has a small family built from one Old English stem.
intro.cn: chew 由一个古英语词干构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, not Latin, so the oldest layers are English and Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，最古老的层次是英语与日耳曼语。

items.meaning: to crush food with the teeth

items.example: He chews on the left side only.
The bread was warm and chewy.
He bought a pack of chewing gum.
His cheek moved as he chewed.

latinEntries.exampleCN: kewwan 变成古英语的 ceowan。

definition_en: a common infectious disease of children that causes a rash of small itchy spots
core_image: 孩子背上冒出一片红点
scene: 一周后男孩身上冒出第一批水痘。A week later the boy showed the first spots of chickenpox.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chickenpox 指水痘；句意是一周后男孩冒出第一批水痘。

senses.title: The disease
senses.definition: a common infectious disease of childhood that causes a spotty rash
senses.definitionCN: 儿童常见的传染病，会出现斑点状皮疹
senses.example: Chickenpox spreads easily between children.
senses.exampleCN: 水痘在孩子之间很容易传播。
senses.why: The name contrasts it with the far worse smallpox.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把它与严重得多的天花区分开。

senses.title: The rash itself
senses.definition: the rash of small itchy spots that the disease produces
senses.definitionCN: 该病引起的细小发痒斑点
senses.example: The chickenpox crusted over within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 水痘疹一周内结了痂。
senses.why: The disease name is also used for its visible rash.
senses.whyCN: 病名也被用来指它看得见的疹子。

intro.en: Chickenpox joins chicken, meaning mild, with pox, a disease of pustules.
intro.cn: chickenpox 由表示「较轻」的 chicken 与指脓疱病的 pox 组合而成。

items.en: Poc means a pustule.
items.cn: poc 意为脓疱。

items.en: Pox names a disease with pustules.
items.cn: pox 指起脓疱的病。

items.en: Chicken pox is named for its milder spots.
items.cn: 十七世纪因斑点较轻而得名。

items.en: Doctors separate it from smallpox.
items.cn: 十八世纪医生把它与天花区分。

items.en: A vaccine is developed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪研发出疫苗。

items.en: The word now names the disease alone.
items.cn: 现代只指这种病本身。

note.en: The look-alike group names other pox diseases; the near-meaning group lists childhood infections.
note.cn: 形近组列出其他痘类疾病；近义组列出儿童传染病。

entries.definition: A deadly pox disease.
A mild pox of cattle.
A disease with pustules.
A viral childhood disease.
A viral infection of the glands.
A mild viral rash.

normalIntro.en: A milder pox, so the old name said chicken.
normalIntro.cn: 因为症状较轻，旧名里才放了「鸡」。

normal.en: Poc means a pustule.
normal.cn: poc 意为脓疱。

normal.en: Pox is a disease of pustules.
normal.cn: pox 是起脓疱的病。

normal.en: Smallpox was the deadly one.
normal.cn: 天花是致命的那个。

normal.en: Chicken marked the milder version.
normal.cn: chicken 用来标记较温和的版本。

normal.en: The spots itch and then crust.
normal.cn: 疹子发痒，随后结痂。

abstract.en: A mild storm of red dots.
abstract.cn: 一场小红点组成的轻风暴。

abstract.en: A week of itching and quarantine.
abstract.cn: 发痒与隔离的一周。

abstract.en: A name that measures danger.
abstract.cn: 用词比较危险的命名。

examples.en: Chickenpox kept him home for a week.
examples.cn: 水痘让他在家待了一周。

examples.en: The chickenpox vaccine is given in two doses.
examples.cn: 水痘疫苗分两剂接种。

examples.en: Adults can catch chickenpox too.
examples.cn: 成人也会感染水痘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鸡啃破」——鸡啃破了皮，留下一片水痘疹。

root: 古英语 poc（脓疱）→ pox；chicken 表示「较轻的」→ chickenpox

sensesIntro.en: One name covers both the illness and the rash it leaves on the skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指疾病，也指它在皮肤上留下的疹子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child back covered in small red spots
core.cn: 核心意象：覆满小红点的孩子后背

branches.en: A school notice about an outbreak.
branches.cn: 学校关于疫情的告示。

branches.en: A thermometer and a quiet bedroom.
branches.cn: 体温计与安静的卧室。

branches.en: Small itchy spots behind the ears.
branches.cn: 耳后发痒的小红点。

branches.en: Scabs drying on a shoulder.
branches.cn: 肩头正在干的痂。

branches.en: A mild pox that writes its name on the skin.
branches.cn: 把名字写在皮肤上的轻痘。

intro.en: Chickenpox carries an old word for pustule; the list below adds words of spots, infection and immunity.
intro.cn: chickenpox 含有表示脓疱的古词；下面列出斑点、感染与免疫词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin variola is a spot and vacca is a cow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 variola 意为斑点，vacca 意为母牛。

latinEntries.example: Variola is the old name for smallpox.
latinEntries.exampleCN: variola 是天花旧称。
vacca 产生 vaccine 与 vaccination。
pustula 产生 pustule 与 pustular。

definition_zh: 首领；酋长；主要的；首席的
definition_en: the leader of a group or an organization, or most important and highest in rank
core_image: 站在队伍最前面的那个人
scene: 会议桌两端坐满了人，屋里渐渐安静。The chief of the village spoke last and everyone listened.
sceneCN: 这里 chief 指「首领」（第 1 个义项：群体或组织的领导者）；句意是村里的首领最后发言，所有人都在听。

senses.title: The leader of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a group, a tribe or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导群体、部落或组织的人
senses.example: The village chief settled the dispute himself.
senses.exampleCN: 村长亲自解决了这场争端。
senses.why: The Latin word for head gave the name of the person at the head of a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「头」的词，给出了站在一群人最前面那个人的称呼。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: most important among several things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中最重要的
senses.example: The chief reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: The head is the top of the body, so the adjective came to mean topmost in importance.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的顶端，因此形容词表示重要性上位居最高。

senses.title: Highest in rank
senses.definition: holding the highest position in a profession or an office
senses.definitionCN: 在某行业或机构中居于最高职位的
senses.example: She was appointed chief engineer of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为该项目的总工程师。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as height, so the head word marks the top post in a title.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高低，因此这个「头」词标记出头衔中的最高职位。

intro.en: Chief is the Latin word for head, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: chief 是拉丁语中表示「头」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Caput meant the head of a person or an animal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 指人或动物的头。

items.en: Chief meant the head, both of a body and of a group.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 既指身体的头，也指群体的头。

items.en: Chief named the leading person of a household or a band.
items.cn: 英语 chief 指家庭或队伍中的领头人。

items.en: The same form began to work as an adjective meaning principal.
items.cn: 同一形式开始作形容词，意为首要的。

items.en: Chief covers leaders, top posts and the most important reason.
items.cn: 如今 chief 涵盖首领、最高职位与最重要的理由。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same long vowel or the same origin, while the meaning group names leaders.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的长元音或同一来源，近义组列出领导者。

entries.definition: the head cook of a kitchen
a person who steals
a community ruled by a chief
a person who guides a group
the person in charge of a group
the most important of several things

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root caput, the chef doublet and the rank sense of chief.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根 caput、同源词 chef 以及 chief 的职位义。

normal.en: Chief and chef are twins: the French form became the cook, the English one the leader.
normal.cn: chief 与 chef 是一对双胞胎：法语形式成了厨师，英语形式成了首领。

normal.en: Chief hides caput, the Latin head, also seen in capital and captain.
normal.cn: chief 里藏着拉丁语「头」caput，capital 与 captain 也含这个词根。

normal.en: A chief is at the head of people; a chief reason is at the head of a list.
normal.cn: chief 是人前的头，也是理由清单上的头。

normal.en: The plural chiefs simply adds an s after two consonants.
normal.cn: 复数 chiefs 只需在词尾加 s。

normal.en: Editor in chief puts the head word after the job, a common newspaper title.
normal.cn: editor in chief 把「头」词放在职务之后，是常见的报纸头衔。

abstract.en: Picture one figure standing a step ahead of a long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在长队前面半步。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to quiet a whole hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，让整个大厅安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate reading chief engineer on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一块写着总工程师的名牌。

examples.en: The chief called the meeting to order.
examples.cn: 首领宣布会议开始。

examples.en: Safety is our chief concern.
examples.cn: 安全是我们最主要的关切。

examples.en: He was chief of the department for ten years.
examples.cn: 他担任该部门主管十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: chief 与 chef 同源，都是「头」：厨房的头是主厨，人群的头是首领。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经古法语 chief 进入英语，既作名词「首领」，也作形容词「首要的」。

sensesIntro.en: The head of a body of people gives the leader, and the head as the topmost part gives both the important and the highest-ranked senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 一群人中的「头」给出首领义，而作为最顶端的「头」给出「主要」与「最高职位」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head of a body, human or social.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体或一个群体的「头」。

branches.en: The leader sense names a person.
branches.cn: 首领义项指一个人。

branches.en: The important sense ranks reasons and aims.
branches.cn: 主要义项给理由与目标排序。

branches.en: The rank sense builds titles such as chief engineer.
branches.cn: 职位义项构成总工程师这类头衔。

branches.en: A chief holds the chief post.
branches.cn: 首领占据最高的职位。

branches.en: Both adjective senses place something at the top.
branches.cn: 两个形容词义项都把某物置于顶端。

intro.en: Chief builds a small family from the Latin head root caput.
intro.cn: chief 从拉丁语「头」词根 caput 出发，构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput, the head, also gives capital, captain and the French chef.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput（头）也给出 capital、captain 以及法语的 chef。

items.example: The land is chiefly used for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用来放牧。

items.example: The chieftain wore a heavy cloak.

items.meaning: a society led by a chief
the leader of a team or a ship

items.exampleCN: caput 是 chief 背后的词。

definition_en: the period of life when a person is a child
core_image: 一张边角卷起的童年合影
scene: 老屋里翻出一本相册，边角已经卷起。Her childhood was spent in a small town by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 childhood 指「童年」（第 1 个义项：身为儿童的时期）；句意是她的童年在河边的一座小镇度过。

senses.title: The time of being a child
senses.definition: the period of a person's life when they are a child
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身为儿童的那段生命时期
senses.example: He spent his childhood on a farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的童年在农场度过。
senses.why: The suffix -hood names a state or a period, so child plus -hood is the time of being a child.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 表示状态或时期，因此 child 加 -hood 就是身为儿童的时期。

senses.title: An early stage of development
senses.definition: the early period in the growth of an idea, an industry or a movement
senses.definitionCN: 某种观念、行业或运动成长中的早期阶段
senses.example: The film industry was still in its childhood then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时电影业还处在萌芽阶段。
senses.why: A young thing passes through a childhood too, so the human period became a metaphor for early growth.
senses.whyCN: 新生事物也会经历「童年」，于是人生的这段时期成了早期发展的比喻。

intro.en: Childhood joins the old word child to the native suffix -hood, which names a state.
intro.cn: childhood 把古词 child 与表示状态的本土后缀 -hood 结合。

items.en: Cild meant a young person.
items.cn: 古英语 cild 指年幼的人。

items.en: The suffix -had named a state or a condition.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -had 表示状态或境况。

items.en: The suffix settled as -hood in words like manhood.
items.cn: 这个后缀在 manhood 等词中定型为 -hood。

items.en: Childhood fixed the sense of the whole period of being young.
items.cn: childhood 固定为「整个年幼时期」的意思。

items.en: The word also describes the early stage of an industry or an idea.
items.cn: 这个词也用来描述行业或观念的早期阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from child, while the meaning group names periods of early life.
note.cn: 形近组由 child 派生，近义组列出生命的早期阶段。

entries.definition: a young person
silly in the way of a child
more than one child
the period when someone is young
the earliest period of life
the time when someone is a boy

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -hood period suffix and the parallel words adulthood and manhood.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示时期的 -hood 后缀以及 adulthood、manhood 这类平行词。

normal.en: Childhood is child plus -hood, the same ending that gives adulthood and manhood.
normal.cn: childhood 是 child 加 -hood，adulthood 与 manhood 也用这个结尾。

normal.en: The suffix -hood names a state or a span of time, never a place.
normal.cn: 后缀 -hood 表示状态或一段时间，从不表示地点。

normal.en: Childhood is uncountable, so you say a happy childhood, not happy childhoods.
normal.cn: childhood 不可数，所以说 a happy childhood，而不用复数。

normal.en: Childhood memories are the scenes that stay after the years go.
normal.cn: childhood memories 是岁月过去后仍留着的画面。

normal.en: An industry in its childhood is young and still experimenting.
normal.cn: 处在 childhood 的行业很年轻，仍在摸索。

abstract.en: Picture a photo album open on a dusty floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一本相册摊在落灰的地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a river town seen from a child's height.
abstract.cn: 想象从孩子的高度看河边小镇。

abstract.en: Picture a small bicycle leaning against a wall for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆小自行车靠墙放了很多年。

examples.en: She had a quiet childhood in the countryside.
examples.cn: 她在乡下度过了安静的童年。

examples.en: Childhood memories of that kitchen still comfort him.
examples.cn: 那间厨房的童年记忆至今让他安心。

examples.en: Electric cars were still in their childhood a decade ago.
examples.cn: 十年前电动汽车还处在萌芽阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: child 加 -hood（表示时期）：当孩子的那些年，就是童年。

root: 由古英语 cild（幼者）加本土后缀 -hood（状态、时期，源自古英语 -had）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix turns a person into a period, and any young thing can borrow that period as a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个后缀把人变成一个时期，而任何新生事物都能借这段时期作比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a span of years seen through a child's eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过孩子的眼睛看到的一段岁月。

branches.en: The personal sense covers the years of youth.
branches.cn: 个人义项涵盖年少的岁月。

branches.en: The metaphor sense describes young industries.
branches.cn: 比喻义项描述年轻的行业。

branches.en: Childhood friends are friends from those years.
branches.cn: childhood friends 是那段岁月结识的朋友。

branches.en: Both senses share the image of an early beginning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「早期开端」的意象。

branches.en: A science in its childhood still makes basic mistakes.
branches.cn: 处于童年期的科学仍会犯基本错误。

intro.en: Childhood is a clean compound of a noun and a period suffix.
intro.cn: childhood 是名词与时期后缀的清晰组合。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin: child is Germanic and -hood comes from Old English -had.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语：child 属日耳曼语，-hood 来自古英语 -had。

items.meaning: the period of being a child
items.exampleCN: 他的童年塑造了他的品味。

items.example: He has a childlike trust in people.
items.exampleCN: 他对人有种孩子般天真的信任。

items.meaning: the period of being an adult
the state of being a man

latinEntries.example: Cild is the first half of childhood.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cild 是 childhood 的前半。

definition_zh: adj. 孩子般的；幼稚的，不懂事的
definition_en: typical of a child; silly in a way that suits a child rather than an adult
core_image: 赌气把玩具摔在地上的孩子
scene: 为这点小事赌气，实在太幼稚了。Sulking over such a small thing is childish.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：childish 指孩子气的；句意是为小事赌气显得幼稚。

senses.title: Of a child
senses.definition: typical of a child, often in a neutral or affectionate way
senses.definitionCN: 孩子特有的，常带中性或亲昵色彩
senses.example: She still has a childish love of sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 她对甜食仍有孩子般的喜爱。
senses.why: The suffix -ish simply means having the nature of.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ish 意为具有…的性质。

senses.title: Immature
senses.definition: silly or unreasonable in a way that adults should have outgrown
senses.definitionCN: 成年人不该再有的任性无理
senses.example: Refusing to speak to her was childish.
senses.exampleCN: 不理她实在幼稚。
senses.why: The neutral sense darkened into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 中性的含义后来染上贬义。

intro.en: Childish is child plus the suffix -ish, meaning of the nature of.
intro.cn: childish 是 child 加词尾 -ish，意为「具有…性质」。

items.en: Cild means a child.
items.cn: cild 意为孩子。

items.en: The spelling settles as child.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写固定为 child。

items.en: The suffix means having the nature of.
items.cn: 词缀意为具有…性质。

items.en: Childish means belonging to a child.
items.cn: 十六世纪意为孩子所特有的。

items.en: The word takes on the sense of immature.
items.cn: 十八世纪带上幼稚的贬义。

items.en: Both the neutral and the critical senses survive.
items.cn: 现代中性义与贬义并存。

note.en: The look-alike group adds other child- suffixes; the near-meaning group names immaturity.
note.cn: 形近组在 child 后接不同词缀；近义组列出「不成熟」的说法。

normalIntro.cn: child 加 -ish 就是「孩子般的」，而常常带着责备。

normal.en: Child is the noun.
normal.cn: child 是名词。

normal.en: -ish means having that nature.
normal.cn: -ish 意为具有那种性质。

normal.en: Childish means like a child.
normal.cn: childish 意为像孩子。

normal.en: Said of adults, it becomes a criticism.
normal.cn: 用在成人身上就成了批评。

normal.en: Said of delight, it stays warm.

abstract.en: A tantrum in an adult coat.
abstract.cn: 成人外套里的耍赖。

abstract.en: A pleasure no one outgrows.
abstract.cn: 没人真能长大的快乐。

abstract.en: A word with two temperatures.
abstract.cn: 一个有两种温度的词。

examples.en: His childish jokes annoyed the whole table.
examples.cn: 他幼稚的笑话让全桌人不快。

examples.en: She gave a childish laugh of delight.
examples.cn: 她发出孩子般开心的笑。

examples.en: It was childish to blame the weather.
examples.cn: 把责任推给天气很幼稚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「柴尔迪士」——像个孩子耍脾气，幼稚。

root: 古英语 cild（孩子）+ -ish（…性质的）→ childish

sensesIntro.en: The same word can describe innocent delight or adult sulking.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既能形容天真的喜悦，也能形容成人的赌气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a toy thrown down mid-tantrum
core.cn: 核心意象：赌气时摔在地上的玩具

branches.en: A child laughing at a paper boat.
branches.cn: 对着纸船大笑的孩子。

branches.en: Hands sticky with sweets.
branches.cn: 沾满糖渍的手。

branches.en: A slammed door over nothing.
branches.cn: 为一点小事摔上的门。

branches.en: Silence used as punishment.
branches.cn: 当作惩罚的沉默。

branches.cn: 同一种行为，或被夸或被责。

juvenis 产生 juvenile 与 rejuvenate。
infans 产生 infant 与 infantile。

definition_zh: 寒意；风寒；使变冷；使寒心
definition_en: a cold feeling, a mild illness caused by cold, or to make something cold
core_image: 打开冰箱门时扑面而来的白气
scene: 夜里风从窗缝里钻进来。A chill ran down his back when the door creaked open.
sceneCN: 这里 chill 指「寒意」（第 1 个义项：突然感到的一阵冷）；句意是门吱呀一开，一股寒意顺着他的背脊而下。

collocations.phrase: send a chill down one's spine

senses.title: A feeling of cold
senses.definition: a sudden cold feeling in the air or in the body
senses.definitionCN: 空气里或身体上突然感到的冷
senses.example: There was a chill in the room before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前屋里有一股寒意。
senses.why: The Old English word for cold named the sensation itself, and that sense remains the core.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中表示冷的词本指这种感觉本身，这一义项始终是核心。

senses.title: To make something cold
senses.definition: to make food or drink cold without freezing it
senses.definitionCN: 让食物或饮料变冷但不结冰
senses.example: Chill the soup for an hour before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前把汤冰一小时。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for causing the sensation in an object.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示为物体制造这种感觉。

senses.title: To frighten or discourage
senses.definition: to make someone feel fear or a sudden loss of hope
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恐惧或突然失去希望
senses.example: The empty streets chilled the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道让来访者心里发凉。
senses.why: Fear is felt as cold running down the back, so the cold word moved into emotion.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧常被感觉为背上一阵冷，于是表示冷的词转入情绪。

intro.en: Chill is an old English word for cold that later took on fear and cooling.
intro.cn: chill 是表示寒冷的一个古英语词，后来兼指恐惧与冷却。

items.en: Kal- named cold and coldness.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kal- 指冷与寒冷。

items.en: Ciele named a cold feeling or a cold illness.
items.cn: 古英语 ciele 指寒冷的感觉或受寒之病。

items.en: Chil kept the sense of a shivering cold.
items.cn: 中古英语 chil 保留「冷得发抖」的意思。

items.en: The noun became a verb meaning to make cold.
items.cn: 名词转为动词，意为使变冷。

items.en: Chill also means to frighten, and chill out means to relax.
items.cn: 如今 chill 也指使人恐惧，而 chill out 意为放松。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names cold and fear.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出寒冷与恐惧。

normal.en: Chill and chilly share one root: chill is the feeling, chilly is the weather.
normal.cn: chill 与 chilly 同根：chill 是感觉，chilly 是天气。

normal.en: Catch a chill is the old phrase for catching a cold.
normal.cn: catch a chill 是「着凉」的旧说法。

normal.en: A chill down the spine mixes cold and fear in one image.
normal.cn: a chill down the spine 把寒冷与恐惧合在一幅画面里。

normal.en: To chill drinks is to cool them; to chill a person is to frighten them.
normal.cn: chill drinks 是让饮料变冷，chill a person 是让人心里发凉。

normal.en: Chill out means relax, a modern and very common use.
normal.cn: chill out 意为放松，是现代极其常见的用法。

abstract.en: Picture white mist rolling out of an open freezer.
abstract.cn: 想象白气从打开冰柜里滚出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rubbing its arms in a cold corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在寒冷的走廊里搓着胳膊。

abstract.en: Picture a hair rising on the back of a neck.
abstract.cn: 想象后颈上汗毛竖起。

examples.en: The ghost story chilled the whole room.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sudden cold that makes the skin tighten.

branches.en: The noun names air or body cold.

branches.en: The verb cools drinks and food.

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the cold root kal- also lies behind cool.

definition_en: a large intelligent African ape that lives in groups and uses tools
core_image: 一只黑猩猩用草棍钓白蚁

senses.title: The African great ape
senses.definition: a large intelligent ape of African forests that uses tools

senses.example: Chimpanzees share food with their group.

definition_zh: n. 裂缝，缝隙；叮当声；v. 发出叮当声
definition_en: a narrow opening or crack; a light ringing sound; to make such a sound
core_image: 月光从墙板的缝隙里漏进来
scene: 月光从墙板的缝隙里漏进来。Moonlight came through a chink in the boards.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chink 指缝隙；句意是月光从墙板缝隙里漏进来。

senses.title: A narrow opening
senses.definition: a narrow crack that lets light or air through
senses.definitionCN: 让光或空气通过的细缝
senses.example: A chink of light showed under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门下有道细缝透出光。
senses.why: This sense is related to the idea of a gap or slit.
senses.whyCN: 这一义与「裂口、狭缝」的概念相关。

senses.title: A light ringing sound
senses.definition: a short light ringing sound, as of glasses or coins
senses.definitionCN: 杯盏或硬币碰出的短促清脆声
senses.example: The chink of coins came from his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他口袋里传来硬币的叮当声。
senses.why: The sound sense is probably imitative.

intro.en: Chink first names a slit, and later a light ringing sound; the sound sense is probably imitative.

normal.en: Light slips through the slit.

abstract.en: Small sounds with sharp edges.

definition_en: a small piece broken off something, a thin fried piece of potato, or a tiny electronic circuit
core_image: 一小块从木头边缘崩落的薄片
scene: 木匠的工作台上散着一层薄木片。He swept the wood chips into a small pile.
sceneCN: 这里 chip 指「碎片」（第 1 个义项：从整块上崩下的小片）；句意是他把木屑扫成一小堆。

senses.title: A small broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece that has broken off a hard material
senses.definitionCN: 从硬质材料上崩落的小片
senses.example: A chip of stone flew up from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一小块石头从路面飞起来。
senses.why: The Old English word named a piece of wood, and the sense widened to any broken fragment.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词指一小片木头，后来扩展到任何碎裂的片段。

senses.title: A fried potato slice
senses.definition: a thin piece of potato fried until crisp or golden
senses.definitionCN: 切成薄片、炸至酥脆或金黄的土豆
senses.example: The children shared a bag of chips.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们分吃了一袋薯片。
senses.why: A slice of potato looks like a wood chip, so the same word was borrowed for food.
senses.whyCN: 一片土豆看起来像木片，于是同一个词被借去指食物。

senses.title: A tiny electronic circuit
senses.definition: a very small piece of silicon carrying an electronic circuit
senses.definitionCN: 承载电子电路的一小片硅
senses.example: The new chip runs twice as fast.
senses.exampleCN: 新芯片的运行速度是原来的两倍。
senses.why: A silicon wafer is cut into small pieces, and each piece kept the name chip.
senses.whyCN: 硅片被切成小块，每一块都沿用了 chip 这个名字。

intro.cn: chip 起初指一小片木头，后来扩展到食物，再扩展到电子元件。
